# smart_metrics.jsonl — Schema Reference

# Generated by: SMART Framework

# Version: 1.0.0

## Purpose

This document is the canonical reference for every field in a
`smart_metrics.jsonl` entry. One JSON object per line. Siddhi appends one
entry after each epic that receives a Satya PASS verdict.

---

## Required Fields

| Field                | Type    | Constraint                   | Description                  |
| -------------------- | ------- | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `task_id`            | string  | `phase-NN-epic-NN`           | Unique epic identifier       |
| `timestamp`          | string  | ISO 8601 UTC                 | When Siddhi logged the entry |
| `agent`              | string  | `Karma` or `Yukti`           | Primary executing agent      |
| `iterations`         | integer | ≥ 1                          | Karma + Yukti loops taken    |
| `auto_errors_caught` | integer | ≥ 0                          | Errors fixed automatically   |
| `satya_result`       | string  | `PASS`, `PARTIAL`, or `FAIL` | Satya final verdict          |
| `validation_method`  | string  | See list below               | Method Satya applied         |
| `loc_generated`      | integer | ≥ 0                          | Lines generated by agent     |
| `loc_manual`         | integer | ≥ 0                          | Lines added by human         |
| `time_seconds`       | integer | ≥ 0                          | Wall-clock seconds for epic  |

## Optional Fields

| Field        | Type   | Description                       |
| ------------ | ------ | --------------------------------- |
| `notes`      | string | Yukti diagnostic or decision note |
| `case_study` | string | Case study identifier             |
| `phase`      | string | Human-readable phase name         |
| `epic_name`  | string | Human-readable epic name          |

## Allowed Values for `validation_method`

- `analytical` — closed-form comparison
- `benchmark` — published reference result
- `cross-validation` — compare to alternate implementation
- `unit-tests` — automated test suite
- `structural` — document completeness check

## Allowed Values for `agent`

- `Karma` — primary builder ran without debugger intervention
- `Yukti` — debugger was the final agent before Satya (implies iterations > 1)

---

## Canonical Example

```json
{
  "task_id": "phase-01-epic-02",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-30T07:15:11Z",
  "agent": "Karma",
  "iterations": 1,
  "auto_errors_caught": 0,
  "satya_result": "PASS",
  "validation_method": "structural",
  "loc_generated": 162,
  "loc_manual": 0,
  "time_seconds": 120,
  "case_study": "framework",
  "phase": "phase-01-pipeline",
  "epic_name": "pipeline-runtime-docs"
}
```

---

## Validation Rules (enforced by `src/smart-metrics/schema.js`)

1. All 10 required fields must be present
2. `task_id` must match `/^phase-\d{2}-epic-\d{2}$/`
3. `timestamp` must be parseable by `new Date()`
4. `agent` must be `"Karma"` or `"Yukti"`
5. `iterations`, `auto_errors_caught`, `loc_generated`, `loc_manual`,
   `time_seconds` must all be non-negative integers
6. `satya_result` must be `"PASS"`, `"PARTIAL"`, or `"FAIL"`
7. `validation_method` must be one of the five values listed above

---

## Notes on JSONL Format

- One valid JSON object per line
- No trailing comma after the last field
- File encoded as UTF-8 with LF line endings
- Each line must be independently parseable by `JSON.parse()`
- Append only — never rewrite existing entries
